hero.cta: Join the Waitlist — Shape What We Build
hero.headline: Most AI productivity apps fail before they ship — here's how to beat the odds
hero.subheadline: Join a waitlist built around research, not hype. Help define the one workflow worth solving first.

problem.body: Research is unambiguous: 'lack of a well-defined use case' tops every survey of why AI projects derail. Not funding. Not talent. Not the model. The use case. Right now, the productivity space is consolidating around Microsoft Copilot, Notion AI, and Google Workspace AI — each with deep enterprise integration and billions in distribution. A vague 'AI for knowledge workers' concept has no procurement path, no differentiated value, and no defense against immediate substitutability. The status quo is not a strategy. It is a countdown to churn.
problem.heading: You have an AI idea. But you don't have a use case. And that is the #1 reason AI startups die.

items.answer: This landing page is designed to test and refine the use case with real users before building — the waitlist itself becomes the research instrument to discover which workflow resonates.
items.question: How can this succeed when research shows AI startups consistently fail without a defined use case?

items.answer: We are not competing as another broad tool — we are starting narrow and will specialize based on waitlist feedback, avoiding the 'generic horizontal agent' trap that research shows leads to churn.
items.question: What distinguishes this from Microsoft Copilot, Notion AI, and Google Workspace AI?

items.answer: Join the waitlist to help define the specific workflow and measurable outcomes — early access members will shape the product's direction and receive priority onboarding for the use case they need most.
items.question: The value proposition is unverifiable — no specific tasks or measurable time savings are defined.

items.answer: We are explicitly avoiding the wrapper trap by validating a specific workflow and building proprietary integration depth before scaling — the waitlist phase ensures we master one use case before expanding.
items.question: Is this just another 'LLM wrapper' with a slick interface but no defensible IP?
